slides.title: SINES OR COSINES? PICK THE RIGHT LAW
THE TWO LAWS
lines: sin A / a = sin B / b = sin C / c
slides.note: Both work on any triangle, not just right triangles.

slides.title: HOW TO PICK
lines: Know an angle and the side opposite it (a matching pair)? Sines.
Know SAS or SSS (no matching pair)? Cosines.
slides.note: Cosines first, then sines finishes the rest.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
steps: A and a are a matching pair, so use sines

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
steps: Two sides and the angle between them (SAS): cosines

slides.title: WATCH OUT
points: SSA can give two triangles, one, or none (the ambiguous case).
Check whether the sine you find is above 1, and whether the supplementary angle also fits.

pageTitle: Law of Sines vs Law of Cosines: Which One to Use and Examples
description: Know when to use the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines for any triangle, with both formulas and two worked examples.
